figure.name: Eduard Bernstein
figure.role: Social democratic theorist of revisionism, elections, unions, reform, and democratic strategy.
figure.hook: Bernstein = democratic reform instead of violent rupture.
whyHere: Bernstein belongs here because he makes the socialism road argue with itself: must capitalism be overthrown all at once, or can democracy, unions, and public law change society step by step?
He matters because a lot of modern social democracy grows out of this question. Reform is not the same thing as surrender, but it also has to prove it can change real power.
figure.cleanIdea: The reform road asks whether democratic institutions can steadily reduce class power without turning politics into civil war.

figure.discussionText: This is the planned debate room for Bernstein: reform, elections, unions, social democracy, revisionism, and whether democracy can change economic power.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: The socialist road splits over democratic reform, unions, elections, and whether capitalism can be transformed without rupture.

ideas.title: Revisionism
ideas.plainDefinition: Revisionism is the argument that socialist theory and strategy should be revised when democratic, economic, and social conditions change.
ideas.context: In the Bernstein path, revisionism means refusing to treat older formulas as sacred when elections, unions, and reform institutions are changing the political field.
ideas.whyMatters: Revisionism matters because it forces the study guide to separate democratic socialist reform from revolutionary seizure of power.

sources.title: Bernstein / Evolutionary Socialism
sources.note: supports: revisionism, movement, and reform strategy.

ideas.title: Democratic Reform
ideas.plainDefinition: Democratic reform means changing society through voting, parties, unions, public law, bargaining, and civil rights instead of immediate armed rupture.
ideas.context: In the Bernstein path, reform is not a side issue. It is the central wager that democracy can be a tool for social change.
ideas.whyMatters: Democratic reform matters because much of modern socialism, labor politics, and welfare-state politics lives on this road.

sources.title: Bernstein / Evolutionary Socialism
sources.note: supports: legislative reform, democratic political action, and the comparison between constitutional legislation and revolutionary force.

ideas.title: Social Democracy
ideas.plainDefinition: Social democracy is a democratic reform tradition that keeps elections and civil rights while expanding labor rights, public services, social insurance, and public accountability.
ideas.context: In the Bernstein path, social democracy is the reform road becoming a durable political tradition.
ideas.whyMatters: Social democracy matters because it is one of the major ways socialist language entered democratic governments without becoming one-party rule.
